Clever Improvisation: How to Keep Your Car Going on Just Three Wheels

By Rain Noe - September 4
in Cars
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 0:45
Instaread

Here we see footage of the Baja Mongolia offroad racing event. The vehicle is a UTV fielded by the GTHub team out of Ulan Bataar.

Now look at it from the other side:

Mid-race, they destroyed their vehicle's front left suspension, severing the connection to the front left wheel. Somehow they found two logs, and used the now-useless front tire and spare tire as counterweights to keep the vehicle going.

Genesis' New Luxury Electric SUV has No B-Pillar, No Start Button, Radiant Floor Heating

By Rain Noe - August 31
in Cars

Genesis, Hyundai's luxury spin-off, has just unveiled their new GV90 Neolun flagship. And it's a doozy. The luxury three-row electric SUV, which has a 311-mile (500km) range, has a feature no competitor has: What used to be called suicide doors, but which are now known as coach doors. Genesis' engineers have figured out how to remove the B-pillar, normally a key structural component, while maintaining safety standards.

Genesis utilized a newly developed dual-motion hinge mechanism for the rear doors, optimized for the vehicle's hidden B-pillar body structure which enables the rear doors to open and close independently without impeding the front doors. This mechanism works by first sliding the rear door slightly outward, then smoothly rotating it open. This enhances the convenience of entering and exiting the vehicle, allowing rear-seat passengers to get in and out with greater space and comfort.

Safety remains paramount in the GV90 Neolun, despite the absence of a B-pillar. Genesis engineered a new structure that seamlessly marries the doors to the vehicle body while maintaining the highest safety standards. Additionally, replacing the conventional B-pillar, high-strength dual steel beams have been integrated for rigidity. This architecture that joins the doors and body effectively disperses collision forces.

A concealed yet robust roll cage is created by reinforcing the passenger cabin with a frame 1.5 times thicker than conventional vehicles and fortifying it with integrated high-strength steel tubes and structural foam. This hidden roll cage structure protects occupants while achieving crash safety performance equivalent to vehicles with conventional B-pillars.

Some other innovative features of the vehicle:

- When the vehicle is parked, the massive center screen can be extended upwards out of the dashboard.

- There's a new roof airbag, "designed to provide effective protection in severe rollover events. In case of a rollover, it deploys rapidly to cover the entire roof glass, preventing occupant ejection and mitigating injuries caused by contact with the roof."

- The doors close themselves when you pull on the handle.

- There's no ignition button. To start the car, you press on the brake pedal.

- The vehicle has freaking radiant heat. The windshield, side panels, door trims, and first- and -second row armrests all generate heat. So does the veneer floor for the second row of seats.

Genesis hasn't yet announced a price, nor released photos of the some of the fancy features we mentioned above; we imagine both are coming soon.
